name: Baked Italian Salmon with Balsamic Tomato-Pepper & Basil Bruschetta

instructions.primary_message: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F) and position rack in the upper third of the oven. Line a baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make clean-up easier (optional).

Place vinegar and sugar in a small saucepan, then bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until reduced by half, 6-7 minutes. Remove balsamic glaze from heat and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
¾ cup balsamic vinegar
1 ½ tbsp brown sugar

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, pat salmon dry with paper towels. Transfer to the baking sheet, drizzle with oil, and season the top side with spices.
instructions.secondary_message:
1.02 kg salmon fillet
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
1 ½ tsp Italian seasoning
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake until salmon is cooked through, 10-12 minutes. Remove from oven.
While the salmon is cooking, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 small pkgs grape tomatoes
1 ½ orange bell peppers
1 small pkg fresh basil

instructions.primary_message: Halve grape tomatoes. Place in a medium bowl.
Trim, seed, and small dice bell peppers. Add to the bowl with the tomatoes.
Pick basil leaves off the stems, roll up crosswise, and thinly slice into ribbons. Add to the bowl.
Peel and mince shallot and garlic. Add both to the bowl along with oil, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine the bruschetta mixture and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 shallot
3 cloves garlic
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
¾ tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: When the salmon is done, change oven to broil on high. (Skip this step if you are using a toaster for the bread.)
Arrange bread on a large baking sheet. Place in the oven and broil, flipping halfway through, until lightly toasted, 1-2 minutes. Remove from oven. (Alternatively, you can use a toaster.)
To serve, divide salmon and toast between plates. Top toast with the bruschetta mixture, drizzle with balsamic glaze, and enjoy!
